note: KakkoiSchool lessons the workbench shows at the moment they matter (plan 198, 'Learning along the way'). Source: github.com/KakkoiDev/izumo-io, content/<kind>/<id>.md with .ja.md beside it; read online at school.kakkoi.dev/lessons/<id>.html. Not copied yet: izumo-io has no licence file.

lessons.when: first launch
lessons.why: The three AI risks before anything else; the workbench's own safety rules build on them.

lessons.when: first launch; and when Pi's answer is marked not verified (G-012)
lessons.why: Never trust an AI: why the harness checks, and why the person still looks.

lessons.when: first launch
lessons.why: Working with AI: a force multiplier, not a replacement.

lessons.when: the person's first requests are short or vague
lessons.why: How to ask: the workbench can point here when a request is too vague to act on.

lessons.when: the person asks why Pi 'did not know' something
lessons.why: Context engineering: Pi only knows what it is shown (the 'Pi sees' panel).

lessons.when: the first time the person edits AGENTS.md or Pi's memory
lessons.why: AGENTS.md as the assistant's memory: the workbench uses exactly this file.

lessons.when: the person repeats the same kind of request
lessons.why: Skills: saved prompts the agent reaches for on its own (the harness's guides).

lessons.when: the person asks for a script or a repeated chore
lessons.why: Making and running scripts with AI.

lessons.when: the first time the person opens terminal Pi
lessons.why: Terminal basics.

lessons.when: later, when a request needs a pipe or a search
lessons.why: Pipes and power tools.

lessons.when: the harness's first commit in a new project
lessons.why: Git basics: the time machine the harness uses on every verified change.

lessons.when: the first push, the first pull request
lessons.why: GitHub and collaboration: remotes, GitHub Flow, pull requests, conflicts.

lessons.when: the first 'put it online' (GitHub Pages) and the first installable PWA
lessons.why: Put it online: account, Pages, installable app; the closest lesson to the stack's deploy block.

lessons.when: a project with two languages goes online
lessons.why: Shipping kakkoi.dev: a static site in two languages on GitHub Pages.

lessons.when: a new project's first page
lessons.why: Web architecture: clients and servers (FastAPI serves, htmx asks).

lessons.when: a new project's first page
lessons.why: Hello world: a file in a browser.

lessons.when: the first template edit
lessons.why: HTML tags: what the Jinja templates are made of.

lessons.when: the first form
lessons.why: HTML forms and blocks: htmx forms are plain forms first.

lessons.when: the first style change
lessons.why: CSS basics, under Basecoat and Tailwind.

lessons.when: a layout or 'the page' request (the page-layout guide)
lessons.why: CSS layout: flexbox, grid, responsive; the bug class behind task 173.

lessons.when: the first dialog or validation message
lessons.why: Forms and dialog: validation the stack returns as a 422 fragment.

lessons.when: the PWA files (manifest, service worker) are touched
lessons.why: Offline: service workers, PWA, caching; the starter ships one.

lessons.when: before the first deploy
lessons.why: Polish: performance, lazy loading, error handling.

lessons.when: the first new route
lessons.why: API endpoints and REST; the stack returns fragments, the ideas hold.

lessons.when: the first migration or table
lessons.why: SQLite: tables, CRUD, schema, foreign keys; the stack's database.

lessons.when: the first login or account feature
lessons.why: Authentication: sessions, cookies, password hashing.

lessons.when: the person asks how the local model works
lessons.why: Ollama and chat: the model Pi runs on.

lessons.when: the first app that calls a model
lessons.why: A full-stack AI app.

lessons.when: the first JavaScript island, or a pyright error the person asks about
lessons.why: TypeScript: why every value has a type (the stack's rule, in Python too).

lessons.when: a new game project
lessons.why: The game course, A09 to A23: LittleJS and p2p-core, the kit's game libraries.

lessons.when: the first multiplayer feature
lessons.why: Other people with no server: p2p-core.

lessons.when: the end of a game project
lessons.why: What we did not build, and what each feature would have cost.

lessons.when: a bug request (the bug guide)
lessons.why: Problem solving: understand before you build; reproduce first (lesson L-008).

lessons.when: the plan for a new feature
lessons.why: Keep things super simple: the stack's one way.

lessons.when: the first refactor
lessons.why: Code quality: works, fast, easy to change.

lessons.when: the first deploy
lessons.why: Shipping is a skill.

lessons.when: the first README or docs request
lessons.why: Documentation is your best friend.

lessons.when: a project's dependencies are updated
lessons.why: Tech entropy: why the kit pins versions.

lessons.when: in 'Learn more'
lessons.why: The 20/80 rule: the stack teaches the 20%.

lessons.when: in 'Learn more'
lessons.why: How to learn.

left_out.t01: Environment setup: the harness installs the tools (uv, Python, Chromium); a stack version would say so.
left_out.t09-t11, t13-t16: JavaScript and CSS depth: htmx and Basecoat replace most of it; listed under 'Learn more'.
left_out.t21, t23: A Node server and a JSON database: the stack uses FastAPI and SQLite (t22, t24).
left_out.t28-t29, t31-t34: React, Next.js, Nest.js: off the stack.
left_out.t37-t39: System design: 'Learn more', for projects that outgrow one machine.
left_out.a02, a08: Antigravity and a personal toolkit: the workbench is the toolkit.
left_out.a10-a11, a13-a22: The rest of the game course, reached from a09.

gaps: Making a GitHub account step by step: a18 has one line ('sign up, it is free'). Missing: the username, two-factor authentication, the free plan.
Connecting this computer to GitHub: gh auth login (or an SSH key); no lesson covers it, and the first push fails without it.
A repository from the workbench: git init, the first commit, gh repo create, public or private, .gitignore for secrets.
Hosting the stack: GitHub Pages serves static files only; a FastAPI app needs a host (still undecided in plan 198).
Python versions of the server lessons (t21-t23 are Node).
